title: Site read swallows any failure (network error, timeout, step deadline) and returns an empty result with no note
evidence: Temp test: domain merge.dev, transport throws ECONNRESET on /about → {findings:[],threads:[],notes:[]}. Same with /about hanging and the step deadline 4s away (request aborted with code 'deadline'): empty, no note, nothing thrown.
scenario: The company site times out or resets on /about, or the step deadline cuts the first request. readSite's `catch { break; }` returns zero findings and zero notes. The loop counts the lookup as done and never reruns it (deepCheck.js:1493 reruns only thrown cut-short errors). The report shows the team pages as read with nothing about the person, so a failed lookup looks clean and the profile is thinner.
fix: In readSite, when openPage throws: if no page was read yet, rethrow (cut-short errors keep code 'deadline' so the loop reruns them; others count as a failed source). If some pages were read, add a note naming the paths that failed. Do the same for the `Date.now() > ctx.deadline - 3000` break: throw a 'deadline' HttpError when nothing was read, otherwise add a partial note.
verifyNote: Reproduced. ECONNRESET gives empty findings with no notes. Worse: a 403 on /about (openPage throws, archiveFallback false) breaks the loop, so /team, which held a matching bio, is never asked. The result is no findings, no note, and a thinner profile.
betterFix: In readSite, take each path's error on its own. A cut-short or resting error with nothing read yet is rethrown (code 'deadline' or retryAt), so the loop reruns it. A 403, 5xx or reset moves on to the next path instead of stopping, and its path goes on a failed list. End with a note naming the paths that could not be read. If every path failed, throw so the source counts as failed. The deadline-3000 break follows the same rule.

title: A robots.txt load cut by the step deadline (or a resting host) becomes a permanent 'robots could not be read' and the page is never opened
evidence: Temp test: robots.txt answers after 2.5s, ctx.deadline is now+1.2s. readOne returns without throwing, with only the note 'did not say whether it allows automated reading … the page was not opened'.
scenario: A tied bio page is planned late in a step, or its host is resting after a 429. cachedEntry rejects with 'Out of time' (code 'deadline') or 'resting', and `.catch(() => null)` turns it into 'unknown'. readOne returns a note and nothing else, so the lookup counts as finished and the loop never retries it. A true career or education page about the person is dropped for the whole check, and the note gives the wrong reason.
fix: In robotsVerdict, catch only real robots failures. Rethrow an error when isCutShort(error) or error.code === 'resting', keeping its retryAt, so openPage and readOne throw and the loop reruns the lookup. Keep 'unknown' for genuine failures such as a 5xx or a refused redirect. Treat the onHop path the same way: a cut-short robots check on a hop should throw, not return 'refused'.
verifyNote: Reproduced. robots.txt answers in 2.5s with a 1.2s deadline: readOne returns only a 'robots file could not be read' note and does not throw, so deepCheck's cut-short rerun never fires. robotsVerdict's .catch(()=>null) also turns 'resting' errors into 'unknown'.
betterFix: robotsVerdict rethrows when isCutShort(error) or the error carries a retryAt or resting code, and keeps 'unknown' for real failures. For onHop, a cut-short robots check should abort the request with a deadline error, not report the hop as refused. readSite should then follow the rule from the first finding for these errors instead of the 'unknown' break.

title: Seed and adverse web questions that need a general web search fall back to news headlines at once, and the backup service is skipped
evidence: Ran 4 keylessSearch calls (the DuckDuckGo allowance outside site searches), then a fifth with needGeneral:true and allowMetered:true. Result: engine gnews, headlinesOnly true, tried ddg resting. searchWeb was called 0 times. retryAt was about 10 min away.
scenario: DuckDuckGo allows 4 searches outside site: queries per 10 min. A check has 8 NEEDS_GENERAL questions. From the fifth on, retryAt is the oldest stamp + 10 min, which is more than maxWaitMs (8 min), so the search never waits. A block's 10-minute cooldown also exceeds 8 min. Education and background are then answered by snippet-less Google News headlines. The backup service is reached only when the news feeds find nothing, so the profile stays thin.
fix: In keylessSearch, when needGeneral is set and no general engine answered, try the metered service before the needGeneral throw and before any non-general engine, when allowMetered holds. Set the wait bound so the 10-minute window fits: default maxWaitMs to at least COOLDOWN_MS plus a margin, or pass the check's own remaining wait budget (maxWaitAgeMs minus the time since the check started) from web.js. Add a test that fills the DuckDuckGo budget and then asks a seed question.
verifyNote: Reproduced. After four DDG searches, a seed with needGeneral and allowMetered went to gnews (headlinesOnly) with searchWeb never called. The wait test fails because retryAt (oldest stamp + 10 min) is over the 8-minute maxWaitMs, and the metered service is tried only after the loop, once news found nothing.
betterFix: In the loop, before the first non-general engine, try the metered service when needGeneral and allowMetered hold and no general engine answered. Then wait (throw SEARCH_RESTING) only when metered is unavailable. Derive maxWaitMs from the check's remaining wait budget instead of a fixed 8 minutes. Add a test that fills the DDG budget and then runs a seed question.

title: A short bio on a team page absorbs the next person's bio as the subject's own (pre-existing)
evidence: extractClaims on a team page (h3 'Jane Roe', 'Co-founder & CEO', a 105-character bio, then h3 'Bob Lee', 'CTO', Bob's bio) with person=subject.hasName. bioText = Jane's sentence followed by 'Bob builds things and has done so for many many years...'
scenario: On a company team page the subject's bio is under 160 characters. In aroundName, the break test `line.length <= 60 && size >= 160` does not fire, so the next heading ('Bob Lee', 'CTO') is skipped and Bob's paragraph is added to the subject's bioText. That text is then shown as the subject's archived bio and compared as their 'claim that changed'.
fix: In aroundName, stop at the next line that another person's name would open: a short line (2 to 4 capitalised words, no sentence punctuation) followed by a looksLikeTitle line, or any short line after the first bio paragraph, whatever size is. Better still, scope the bio to the DOM block (closest card or section) that holds the name. Add this two-person page as a test.
verifyNote: Reproduced with extractClaims(person 'Jane Roe'). bioText comes back as Jane's sentence plus Bob's whole bio ('...he holds a PhD'). The heading break needs size >= 160, so after a short bio the next person's name line and title line are skipped.
betterFix: In aroundName, stop at a short name-like line (2-4 capitalised words, no sentence punctuation) whose next line passes looksLikeTitle, whatever the size. Better, scope the bio to the DOM element (card or section) holding the name. Fix together with web-bio-pronoun-dropped, since loosening that filter makes this bleed worse.

title: Swedish, Turkish, Finnish and other names with ö, ä or ü get the German pack instead of their own
scenario: For a Swedish founder (Zennström), the check runs German adverse queries on the German Google News edition. The report says 'lawsuits ... reported in German' were searched. Swedish press (sv) and Turkish press (tr) are never asked. FIRST_NAMES.de even lists 'björn'. The sv pack fires only on 'å', and tr only on ğ, ı or ş.
fix: Treat ä, ö and ü as ambiguous: count them for German only when no other language's letters, first name, place or domain spoke, as is done for 'é'. Test the more specific signs first (sv: å or Swedish names; tr: ğ, ı, ş, ç plus Turkish names; fi: names). Drop björn and bjoern from FIRST_NAMES.de and add Nordic and Turkish first-name lists. Add tests for these three names.
verifyNote: Reproduced. Björn Ström, Niklas Zennström and Gökhan Öztürk all give ['de']: the de letters include ö and ü, and the sv/tr letter tests miss these names. The result is a wasted German pass at prior 0.4 and no Swedish or Turkish pass. It does not claim a search that was never run, so the severity is lower.
betterFix: Count ä, ö and ü for German only when no other sign spoke, as is already done for é. Add sv/tr first-name lists, move björn to sv, and add ç and ö-with-Turkish-name signs for tr. Test these three names.

title: The Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Hebrew and Hindi packs search the Latin-script name, which local press does not print
evidence: webTemplates for 'Masayoshi Son' with place Japan gives '"Masayoshi Son" (訴訟 OR 詐欺 OR ...)'. In GDELT, withoutShortWords reduces this to '"Masayoshi Son"' because every CJK term has two characters.
scenario: Japanese press writes 孫正義, not 'Masayoshi Son', so the quoted Latin phrase plus Japanese terms finds little or nothing. The lookup is recorded as searched ('lawsuits and fraud allegations in the Japanese-language press') with no finding, which reads as clean. The same holds for ko, zh, he and hi. The zh pack is Simplified Chinese with the CN edition even for a Taiwan or Hong Kong subject.
fix: For non-Latin packs, search the subject's name in that script when one is known (subject.variants or aliases from Wikidata labels), e.g. ('"孫正義"' OR '"Masayoshi Son"'). With no native-script name, either skip the pack or return partial: ['<lang> press: name known only in Latin script'] so it is not counted as searched. Add a zh-TW edition with Traditional terms for tw and hk. Never send a CJK adverse query to GDELT, which drops the terms.
verifyNote: The ja/ko/zh/he/hi packs put the quoted Latin name in front of native-script terms. Local press writes the native name, so recall is poor while the lookup is still tallied as general. The GDELT point does not apply: adverse-<lang> is a web query, and GDELT is only in the news order.
betterFix: Use a native-script name from subject aliases or Wikidata labels when one exists ('"孫正義" OR "Masayoshi Son"'). Without one, return partial (name known only in Latin script) and do not count the pack as searched. The zh-TW edition is optional.

title: Spelling variants of one degree are still reported as a medium 'degree changed'
evidence: compareClaims for the same school gives changed/degree/medium for: 'AB, Economics' vs 'A.B., Economics'; 'Juris Doctor (J.D.)' vs 'JD'; 'Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.), Mechanical' vs 'BEng, Mechanical Engineering'; "Bachelor's degree" vs 'BA, Economics'; 'Master of Business Administration - MBA' vs 'MBA, Finance'.
scenario: LinkedIn rewrites the same credential over the years. Each case above appears in the report as a medium-severity credential claim that changed. The fix covers only the two audit test pairs: TITLE_SYNONYMS handles 'b a', 'b s' and 'm s', but not 'a b', 'j d', 'b eng', 'juris doctor' or 'bachelor of engineering'. A field added to a degree with none ('Bachelor's degree' becoming 'BA, Economics') also counts as a change.
fix: Normalise every dotted or spaced abbreviation (collapse single letters: 'a b' to 'ab', 'j d' to 'jd', 'b eng' to 'beng'). Map 'juris doctor' to 'jd' and 'bachelor/master of engineering' to beng/meng. In sameDegree, treat a field present on one side and absent on the other as the same degree when the levels agree (report it as info at most). Add these pairs as tests.
verifyNote: Reproduced. AB vs A.B., Juris Doctor (J.D.) vs JD, B.Eng. vs BEng, Bachelor's degree vs BA Economics, and MBA vs MBA, Finance all come back as changed/degree/medium. Only the b a, b s and m s spacings are normalised.
betterFix: Collapse runs of single letters in normText ('a b'->'ab', 'j d'->'jd', 'b eng'->'beng'). Map juris doctor to jd and bachelor/master of engineering to beng/meng, and add jd/md to a professional kind. In sameDegree, when the levels agree and one side has no field, return same, or report it as info only.

title: The new 'names them' filter drops real bio changes on the person's team or personal page when the bio says 'she' or 'I'
evidence: extractClaims on a team page block under 'Jane Roe' gives a bioText with no name in it ('Before co-founding Acme, she spent six years ... at Stripe'). compareClaims against 'She is a former Goldman Sachs banker ... MBA from Wharton' gives bio/changed. namesThem(before) and namesThem(after) are both false, so line 577 drops it.
scenario: aroundName takes the bio from the lines after the person's own name and title, so it rarely repeats the name. Third-person bios ('she previously...') and first-person ones on a personal site ('I previously...') are therefore all discarded on 'page' format. That includes a real change of employer or a newly claimed MBA, which is a true claim change hidden from the report.
fix: Skip the namesThem test when the bio came from aroundName anchored on the subject's own name (claims.named === true, or the bio block follows the subject's name line). Keep the filter only for bios not anchored to the name, such as an og:description or a blog author box that names someone else. Alternatively, accept a bio that opens with a pronoun or 'I' on a page whose name line is the subject's.
verifyNote: aroundName gives 'Before co-founding Acme, she spent six years...' with no name in it. namesThem looks only for the full name or first name, so on 'page' format both sides fail and a real bio change is dropped.
betterFix: Have aroundName mark its bio as anchored to the subject's name (for example bioAnchored: true), and skip the namesThem filter for anchored bios. This is safe only after the team-page bleed is fixed. Otherwise anchored bios would carry the neighbour's text into the comparison.

title: A degree hidden by asterisks on an older copy shows as 'degree added' (medium) on the next unmasked copy
evidence: Read changeFindings: from(field) falls back to prev when lastWith.education is null, and prev can be masked. unmask() turns '****** *****' into ''. compareClaims('', 'PhD, Chemistry') gives added/degree/medium (reproduced). The downgrade applies only when cur.claims.masked.
scenario: A profile's first archived copy is a 2024 signed-out view with masked degree lines; the next copy shows 'PhD, Chemistry, Stanford'. The PhD is reported as a medium 'degree added', which reads as credential inflation, though the older copy only hid it.
fix: In changeFindings, skip degree 'added' changes when the older source copy (from('education')) is masked, or drop them to info. More generally, mark a degree as unknown (null), not '' (none stated), when it was masked or came only from the JSON-LD alumniOf fallback, and never diff an unknown degree.
verifyNote: Confirmed by reading the code, not by a test. lastWith is never set from a masked copy, so with only masked earlier copies, from('education') returns the masked prev. The downgrade checks only cur.claims.masked, so a degree hidden on the older copy shows as a medium 'added'.
betterFix: In changeFindings, when from(d.field).claims.masked (the older source), skip degree 'added' changes or set them to info. Also treat a masked degree as unknown, not '', in compareClaims.
